title: Lower-bound induction on k for IMO 1985 Q2
intent: Prove that every number k * j % n (for 1 ≤ k < n) has the same color as j by induction on k over the lower bound 1 ≤ k, so that the base is k = 1 and the step inherits the strengthened bound 1 ≤ k < n needed to apply the induction hypothesis.

parent.name: C_mul_mod
parent.statement:
lemma C_mul_mod {n j : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hj : j ∈ Set.Ico 1 n) (cpj : Nat.Coprime n j)
    {C : ℕ → Fin 2} (hC : Condition n j C) {k : ℕ} (hk : k ∈ Set.Ico 1 n) :
    C (k * j % n) = C j := by

children.name: step (k → k + 1)
children.statement: C ((k + 1) * j % n) = C j with hk₁ : 1 ≤ k and hk.2 : k + 1 < n
children.closed_by: rw [← ih ⟨hk₁, Nat.lt_of_succ_lt hk.2⟩, hC.2 _ b₁ nej]; rcases nej.lt_or_gt with h | h; the two branches close by rewrite chains reducing |j − (k+1)*j % n| to k*j % n

applicability.goal_shape: ∀ k, k ∈ Set.Ico m n → P (f k), a statement about f k to be proved for k in a half-open interval [m, n) with nonzero lower bound m (here m = 1, f k = k * j % n)
applicability.use_when: the induction variable has a nonzero lower bound and the step must apply the induction hypothesis at the previous value k, which still satisfies m ≤ k < n; Nat.le_induction sets the base at the lower bound and carries the bound m ≤ k into the step
applicability.avoid_when: the lower bound is 0 (plain induction k suffices); the step needs the IH at an index outside [m, n) so the strengthened bound does not reach; or the step's own case analysis dominates the induction, in which case it should be factored into a separate lemma

claims.claim: C_mul_mod is proved entirely by induction on the lower bound (induction k, hk.1 using Nat.le_induction): the base goal closes in one rewrite (line 53) and the step goal closes inline (lines 54-77), with no auxiliary lemma stated.

claims.claim: The authors state the informal plan the induction follows: 'it suffices to show that kj mod n ∼ (k−1)j mod n for 1 < k < n', with the two cases 'if kj mod n > j' and 'if kj mod n < j', and the lemma's doc comment states 'For 1 ≤ k < n, k * j % n has the same color as j'.
C_mul_mod is used exactly once, in the theorem result at line 92 (rw [hvi, C_mul_mod hn hj cpj hC vib]), which closes the main result.
The step's two arithmetic branches are asymmetric: the (k+1)*j % n < j branch is 9 lines (67-75) and the j < (k+1)*j % n branch is 2 lines (76-77).
claims.evidence: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/e1545ebed97594477bbd88b2fe948ffce56e5af2/Archive/Imo/Imo1985Q2.lean#L66-L77, counted by hand over the copied file

metrics.how_counted: lines 49-77 of the copied file; induction children = the base and step goals of Nat.le_induction; step branches = the two goals of rcases nej.lt_or_gt; the haves nej and b₁ are inline, not top-level lemmas

consequences: Induction on hk.1 with Nat.le_induction sets the base at the lower bound (k = 1, not k = 0) and carries 1 ≤ k into the step, so the step is stated for k + 1; the upper bound is generalised (the step sees hk.2 : k + 1 < n), which is what lets the IH be applied at ⟨hk₁, Nat.lt_of_succ_lt hk.2⟩. The step must then establish nej : (k+1)*j % n ≠ j (from coprimality) and b₁ : (k+1)*j % n ∈ Set.Ico 1 n before rule 2 (hC.2) can apply, and finally split on nej.lt_or_gt; each branch does a different arithmetic reduction of |j − (k+1)*j % n| to k*j % n. Failure modes: if the step needs the IH at an index outside [1, n) the strengthened bound does not reach; if j is not coprime the nej step fails; the two branches need separate, non-uniform rewrite work.
